pencereler.0-5: As a DC-10 lifted off from Chicago, its left engine tore away. The jet
pencereler.5-12: rolled over and crashed, killing everyone aboard and two on the ground. The damage had been done weeks earlier,
pencereler.12-20: during maintenance. To save time, workers removed engine and pylon together with a forklift. That cracked the pylon's mounting. At take-off, it
pencereler.20-30: broke and cut hydraulic lines. The slats on one wing retracted, and that wing stalled. The shortcut was banned, and slats got protection against retracting.

segmentler.metin: American Airlines Flight 191 crashed after an engine tore off at take-off.
It took only a maintenance shortcut that cracked the engine pylon.
So how could a maintenance shortcut that cracked the engine pylon do this?
The answer is pylon bulkhead cracked by removing engine and pylon together with a forklift — and it is why the shortcut was banned and slat systems were given locking protection.
